taxonomy.note: Current Kew accepts Salvia azurea at species rank. Central Texas material is often treated regionally as var. grandiflora; preserve that as infraspecific/historical context rather than a duplicate learner taxon.

evidence: Hays — documented on a Hays County native-plant inventory and in the Hays source pool.
Travis — Balcones Canyonlands Preserve list and Travis County herbarium material.
Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center county treatment under Salvia azurea var. grandiflora.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Source-pool membership and iNaturalist counts were not used by themselves as proof.

morphology.look_here_first: Look at stature and leaves: a tall perennial with narrow linear-lanceolate leaves and an elongated flowering axis. Then inspect the green, hairy but not mealy/felted calyx.
diagnostic_traits: often much taller than the small spring sages
opposite narrow linear-lanceolate to linear-oblanceolate leaves
long terminal interrupted panicle of verticils

confusers.separator: Azure sage has a green, normally hairy calyx; mealy blue sage has conspicuously mealy/felty whitish or purplish calyces.
S. azurea is usually much taller with a long open flowering axis; S. engelmannii is a low dense clump with many short stems.
